steps.name: Load, QC, and filter count matrix
caveats: Salmon counts may be non-integer (fractional assignment) — round or use appropriate DESeq2 import handling if needed
Verify metadata column names exactly (condition, time, time_hours) before building the design formula
steps.context: Input files are counts.csv (12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene id) and metadata.csv (12 samples x condition, time, time_hours). Single batch, 3 reps per condition x time cell.
steps.question: Are the salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata (condition, time, time_hours) consistent, and which genes pass a minimum-expression filter for differential testing?
constraints: Do not assume gene IDs are already HGNC symbols — check the counts.csv row identifier format before any downstream annotation step
Keep raw integer counts intact for DESeq2 (do not pre-normalize here)
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12000 x 12) and metadata (12 x 4) load without row/column mismatch; sample IDs align between the two files
Low-count genes filtered (e.g. sum across samples < 10, or edgeR filterByExpr-style rule) with the number of genes retained reported
Library size / total count per sample reported to flag any outlier sample before modeling

steps.name: Fit interaction model: condition x time on treatment response
caveats: With n=3 per cell (12 samples total), power to detect a moderate interaction effect is limited — report this explicitly rather than treating a non-significant interaction as proof of 'no difference'
If dispersion estimates are unstable due to small sample size, note this in the output rather than silently forcing significance calls
steps.context: 2x2 design: 2 conditions x 2 time points (t0,t1), n=3 per cell, 12 samples total, single batch. Using pydeseq2 (available in sandbox) to fit the full interaction model on raw Salmon counts.
steps.question: Does the effect of condition (treatment) on gene expression differ between time point t0 and t1, i.e. is the condition:time interaction term significant, and how do the simple treatment effects at t0 and t1 compare?
constraints: Use raw (filtered, unnormalized) counts as pydeseq2 input; let DESeq2's internal normalization (median-of-ratios) handle library size

Explicitly test the interaction coefficient, not just two separate condition contrasts at each time — the research question is about interaction, and pairwise contrasts without the interaction term risk overclaiming a time-dependent effect that is not statistically supported
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 model fit with design ~condition+time+condition:time on filtered raw counts from T1S1
Interaction term (condition:time) results table produced with log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per gene
Simple treatment-effect contrasts extracted separately for t0 and t1 (e.g. via contrast vectors or model re-leveling) so effect sizes at each time point can be compared directly
Number of genes with significant interaction (padj < 0.05) reported, plus counts of genes significant for treatment at t0 only, t1 only, or both
Diagnostic plots (PCA of normalized counts, dispersion estimates) produced to confirm model fit is reasonable given the single batch, 3-replicate design

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on interaction-significant genes
caveats: Enrichment on a small, underpowered interaction gene set can produce unstable or non-reproducible pathway calls — treat any hits as hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory
WikiPathways gene sets are curated and biased toward well-studied pathways; absence of enrichment does not mean absence of biological effect
steps.context: Reference data available: WikiPathways human gene sets (GMT, HGNC symbols) at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, and a human UniProt ID mapping table for identifier conversion if the count matrix uses Ensembl or UniProt IDs instead of symbols.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes whose treatment effect differs significantly between t0 and t1 (interaction-significant genes), versus genes with a consistent treatment effect across both time points?
constraints: Confirm gene identifier space in counts.csv before choosing whether ID mapping is needed — do not assume symbols match WikiPathways HGNC gene symbols without checking a sample of IDs
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g. hypergeometric/Fisher or GSEA-style) run separately on (a) the interaction-significant gene set from T1S2 and (b) genes significant for treatment at both time points (consistent effect), using the human WikiPathways gene sets found in the reference store
Report which pathways are specific to the time-dependent (interaction) gene set versus the time-independent set
If gene identifiers in counts.csv are not HGNC symbols, map them via the human UniProt ID mapping reference before running enrichment, and report the fraction of genes successfully mapped

If the interaction gene set is empty or too small for meaningful enrichment (a real possibility given the small-sample power caveat), report that explicitly rather than lowering the threshold post hoc to force a result

plan.title: Time x treatment interaction DE in bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq design (condition x time: t0/t1, 3 replicates per cell, 12 samples, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes). The research question - does the treatment effect differ between time points - is a statistical interaction question, best answered with a single DESeq2 model containing condition, time, and their interaction term, rather than two separate pairwise contrasts. Plan: (1) load counts+metadata, QC and filter low-count genes; (2) fit a DESeq2 model with ~condition+time+condition:time and extract the interaction coefficient, plus the simple treatment effects within each time point for interpretability; (3) run pathway enrichment on the interaction-significant genes using the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the reference store; (4) summarize whether the treatment effect is time-dependent, with effect sizes and FDR-corrected significance at each stage, and flag the small n (3/group) that limits power to detect small interaction effects.
